questions.q: For a reversible reaction $\text{R} \rightleftharpoons \text{P}$, at constant temperature, both the forward and the backward reactions are first order elementary reactions with rate constants $k_f$ and $k_b$, respectively. At time zero, the concentration of $\text{R}$ is $[\text{R}]_0$ and the concentration of $\text{P}$ is zero. At any given time, $[\text{R}]$ and $[\text{P}]$ are the concentrations of $\text{R}$ and $\text{P}$, respectively. If $k_b = 4k_f$, the correct graphical representation of the reaction is
questions.solution:
For the reversible first-order reaction $\text{R} \rightleftharpoons \text{P}$, at equilibrium, the rate of the forward reaction equals the rate of the backward reaction.

$k_f [\text{R}]_{eq} = k_b [\text{P}]_{eq}$

Given $k_b = 4k_f$, we can substitute this into the equilibrium condition:

$k_f [\text{R}]_{eq} = 4k_f [\text{P}]_{eq}$

$[\text{R}]_{eq} = 4[\text{P}]_{eq}$

From the conservation of mass, the total concentration remains constant at any time $t$:

$[\text{R}]_{eq} + [\text{P}]_{eq} = [\text{R}]_0$

Substituting $[\text{R}]_{eq} = 4[\text{P}]_{eq}$ into the mass balance equation gives:

$4[\text{P}]_{eq} + [\text{P}]_{eq} = [\text{R}]_0$

$5[\text{P}]_{eq} = [\text{R}]_0$

$[\text{P}]_{eq} = 0.2[\text{R}]_0$

Using this to find $[\text{R}]_{eq}$:

$[\text{R}]_{eq} = 4 \times 0.2[\text{R}]_0 = 0.8[\text{R}]_0$

Therefore, as $t \to \infty$, the concentration ratio $\dfrac{[\text{P}]}{[\text{R}]_0}$ approaches $0.2$ and $\dfrac{[\text{R}]}{[\text{R}]_0}$ approaches $0.8$. This is correctly represented in the third graph.

questions.q: For a first-order reaction $\text{R} \longrightarrow \text{P}$ at a given temperature, $k$ is the rate constant. For this reaction, at the given temperature, the concentrations of $\text{R}$ and $\text{P}$ at a time $t$ are $[\text{R}]$ and $[\text{P}]$, respectively. The correct graphical representation(s) for this reaction is(are)
questions.solution:
For a first-order reaction $\text{R} \rightarrow \text{P}$, the rate law is given by:

$-\dfrac{\text{d}[\text{R}]}{\text{d}t} = \dfrac{\text{d}[\text{P}]}{\text{d}t} = k[\text{R}]$

Integrating this, the concentration of the reactant at time $t$ is $[\text{R}] = [\text{R}]_0 e^{-kt}$.

The concentration of the product at time $t$ is $[\text{P}] = [\text{R}]_0 - [\text{R}] = [\text{R}]_0 (1 - e^{-kt})$.

The plot of $[\text{P}]$ versus $t$ follows the equation $[\text{P}] = [\text{R}]_0 (1 - e^{-kt})$. This represents a curve that starts from the origin and is concave down, approaching a constant value $[\text{R}]_0$. The graph in (A) is concave up, making it incorrect.

The plot of $\dfrac{\text{d}[\text{R}]}{\text{d}t}$ versus $[\text{R}]$ follows the equation $\dfrac{\text{d}[\text{R}]}{\text{d}t} = -k[\text{R}]$. This is a straight line passing through the origin with a negative slope ($-k$). The graph in (B) has a positive slope, making it incorrect.

The plot of $\dfrac{\text{d}[\text{P}]}{\text{d}t}$ versus $t$ follows the equation $\dfrac{\text{d}[\text{P}]}{\text{d}t} = k[\text{R}]_0 e^{-kt}$. This represents an exponentially decreasing curve with respect to time. The graph in (C) matches this behavior, making it correct.

The rate constant $k$ depends only on the temperature and is independent of time. Therefore, the plot of $k$ versus $t$ is a horizontal straight line. The graph in (D) matches this, making it correct.

questions.q:
Consider a reaction $A+R \rightarrow$ Product. The rate of this reaction is measured to be $k[A][R]$. At the start of the reaction, the concentration of $R,[R]_0$, is 10 -times the concentration of $A,[A]_0$. The reaction can be considered to be a pseudo first order reaction with assumption that $k[R]=k^{\prime}$ is constant. Due to this assumption, the relative error (in \%) in the rate when this reaction is $40 \%$ complete, is _______
[ $k$ and $k^{\prime}$ represent corresponding rate constants]
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \qquad \quad \mathrm{A}+\mathrm{R} \rightarrow \text{ Product } \\ & \mathrm{t}=0 \quad \mathrm{ A}_0 \quad 10 \mathrm{ A}_0 \\ & \mathrm{t}=\mathrm{t} \quad 0.6 \mathrm{ A}_0 \quad 9.6 \mathrm{ A}_0 \\ & \text{ Rate }=\mathrm{k}[\mathrm{A}][\mathrm{R}] \\ & \text{ Rate }_1=\mathrm{k}\left(0.6 \mathrm{ A}_0\right) \times 9.6 \mathrm{ A}_0 \\ & \qquad \quad \mathrm{ A} \quad+\quad \mathrm{R} \rightarrow \text{ Product }  \\ & \mathrm{t}=0 \quad \mathrm{ A}_0 \qquad 10 \mathrm{ A}_0(\text{ excess }) \\ & \mathrm{t}=\mathrm{t} \quad 0.6 \mathrm{ A}_0 \quad 10 \mathrm{ A}_0 \\ & \text{ Rate }=\mathrm{k}^{\prime}[\mathrm{A}], \mathrm{k}^{\prime}=\mathrm{k}[\mathrm{R}] \\ & \text{ Rate }_2=\left(\mathrm{k} \times 10 \mathrm{ A}_0\right) \times\left(0.6 \mathrm{ A}_0\right) \\ & 100 \times \frac{\Delta \text{ Rate }}{\text{ Rate }_1}=\frac{(0.6 \times 10-0.6 \times 9.6}{0.6 \times 9.6} \times 100=4.1666\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
A sample initially contains only U-238 isotope of uranium. With time, some of the U-238 radioactively decays into $\mathrm{Pb}-206$ while the rest of it remains undisintegrated.
When the age of the sample is $\mathbf{P} \times 10^8$ years, the ratio of mass of $\mathrm{Pb}-206$ to that of $\mathrm{U}-238$ in the sample is found to be 7 . The value of $\mathbf{P}$ is ______
[Given: Half-life of U-238 is $4.5 \times 10^9$ years; $\log _c 2=0.693$ ]
questions.solution:
${ }_{92} \mathrm{U}^{238} \quad \longrightarrow \quad{ }_{82} \mathrm{~Pb}^{206}+8{ }_2 \mathrm{He}^4+6_{-1} \beta^0$
$\mathrm{t}=0 \quad \mathrm{~N}_0=\left(\frac{1}{238}+\frac{7}{206}\right)$ moles $\mathrm{t}=\mathrm{tN}_{\mathrm{t}}=\frac{1}{238}$ moles $\mathrm{x}=\frac{7}{206}$ moles
Life of sample \(\rightarrow t\) years
\([A]_0 \propto\) Initial mole of \(\mathrm{U}-238\)
\([A]]_t \propto\) Final mole of U-238
\(\begin{aligned}
& \frac{|A|_0}{|A|_t}=\frac{\frac{1}{228}+\frac{7}{206}}{\frac{1}{238}} \\
& =\frac{0.0042+0.0340}{0.0042} \\
& =9.1 \\
& =\frac{2.303 \log 2 \times t}{4.5 \times 10^9}=2.303 \log 9.1 \\
& t=14.27 \times 10^9 \text{ years } \\
& =142.7 \times 10^8 \text{ years } \\
& P=142.7 \\
& P=143
\end{aligned}\)

questions.q:
Consider the following reaction,
$2 \mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{~g})+2 \mathrm{NO}(\mathrm{g}) \rightarrow \mathrm{N}_2(\mathrm{~g})+2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}(\mathrm{g})$
which follows the mechanism given below:
$2 \mathrm{NO}(\mathrm{g}) \stackrel{k_1}{\underset{k_{-1}}{\rightleftharpoons}} \mathrm{N}_2 \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{~g})$ $\quad$ (fast equlibrium)
$\mathrm{N}_2 \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{~g})+\mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{~g}) \xrightarrow{k_2} \mathrm{~N}_2 \mathrm{O}(\mathrm{g})+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}(\mathrm{g})$ $\quad$(slow reaction)
$\mathrm{N}_2 \mathrm{O}(\mathrm{g})+\mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{~g}) \xrightarrow{k_3} \mathrm{~N}_2(\mathrm{~g})+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}(\mathrm{g})$ $\quad$ (fast reaction)
The order of the reaction is_____
questions.solution:
Rate law $=\mathrm{k}_2\left[\mathrm{~N}_2 \mathrm{O}_2\right]\left[\mathrm{H}_2\right] \quad[\because$ slowest step of reaction is RDS $]$
$\because \frac{\mathrm{k}_1}{\mathrm{k}_{-1}}=\frac{\left[\mathrm{N}_2 \mathrm{O}_2\right]}{[\mathrm{NO}]^2}$
$\therefore \quad\left[\mathrm{N}_2 \mathrm{O}_2\right]=\frac{\mathrm{k}_1}{\mathrm{k}_{-1}}[\mathrm{NO}]^2$
$\therefore \quad$ Rate $=\mathrm{k}_2 \times \frac{\mathrm{k}_1}{\mathrm{k}_{-1}}[\mathrm{NO}]^2\left[\mathrm{H}_2\right]$
$\therefore$ Order of reaction is (3)

The plot of ${logk}_{f}$ versus $\dfrac{1}{T}$ for a reversible reaction $A ( g ) ⇌ P ( g )$ is shown.

Pre-exponential factors for the forward and backward reactions are ${10}^{15}{s}^{- 1} and {10}^{11}{s}^{- 1}$, respectively. If the value of $logK$ for the reaction at $500K$ is $6$, the value of $\left|{logk}_{b}\right|$ at $250K$ is
$\left[K =\right$equilibrium constant of the reaction, {k}_{f} =$rate constant of forward reaction, {K}_{b} =$rate constant of backward reaction]
questions.solution:
From the question
$\begin{cases}{A}_{f} = {10}^{15}, {A}_{b} = {10}^{11}, & f = \text{Forward reaction} \\ logK\text{at}500K = 6 & b = \text{Backward reaction} \\ {logk}_{f}\text{at}500K = 9\text{(from graph)} & \\ {logk}_{b}\text{at}500K: & \\ logK = log\left(\dfrac{{k}_{f}}{{k}_{b}}\right)\text{since} ⇒ K = \dfrac{{k}_{f}}{{k}_{b}} & \end{cases}$

$6 = {logk}_{f} - {logk}_{b}$

$6 = 9 - {logk}_{b}$

$log ⁡ {k}_{b} = 3\text{at}500K$

$log ⁡ \dfrac{{k}_{2}}{{k}_{1}} = \dfrac{- {E}_{a}}{R}\left(\dfrac{1}{{T}_{2}} - \dfrac{1}{{T}_{1}}\right)$

${k}_{b} = {A}_{b}e\dfrac{- {E}_{ab}}{RT}$

$ln ⁡ {k}_{b} = ln ⁡ \left({A}_{b}e\dfrac{- {E}_{ab}}{RT}\right)$

${lnk}_{b} = {lnA}_{b} - \dfrac{{E}_{ab}}{RT}$

$2 . 303{logk}_{b} = 2 . 303{logA}_{b} - \dfrac{{E}_{ab}}{500R}$

$\dfrac{{E}_{a}}{500R} = 2 . 303\left({logA}_{b} - {logk}_{b}\right)$

$\dfrac{{E}_{a}}{500R} = 2 . 303\left(log{10}^{11} - 3\right)$

$\dfrac{{E}_{a}}{500R} = 2 . 303 ( 11 - 3 ) = 2 . 303 \times 8$

${E}_{a} = 2 . 303 \times 8 \times 500R$

$ln\left(\dfrac{{k}_{2}}{{k}_{1}}\right) = \dfrac{- {E}_{a}}{R}\left(\dfrac{1}{{T}_{2}} - \dfrac{1}{{T}_{1}}\right)$

$ln\left(\dfrac{{k}_{250K}}{{k}_{500K}}\right) = \dfrac{- {E}_{a}}{R}\left(\dfrac{1}{250} - \dfrac{1}{500}\right)$

$ln\left(\dfrac{{k}_{250K}}{{k}_{500K}}\right) = \dfrac{- 2 . 303 \times 8 \times 500R}{R}\left(\dfrac{1}{500}\right)$

$2 . 303\left({logk}_{250K} - {logk}_{500K}\right) = - 2 . 303 \times 8$

${logk}_{250K} - 3 = - 8$

${logk}_{250K} = - 5$

$\left|{logk}_{250K}\right| = 5$

questions.q: Match the rate expressions in LIST-I for the decomposition of \(\mathrm{X}\) with the corresponding profiles provided in LIST-II. \(X_s\) and \(\mathrm{k}\) are constants having appropriate units.
options: $I \to P; II \to Q; III \to S; IV \to T$
$I \to R; II \to S; III \to S; IV \to T$
$I \to P; II \to Q; III \to Q; IV \to R$
$I \to R; II \to S; III \to Q; IV \to R$
questions.solution:
$\left(I\right)$ rate $= \dfrac{k\left[X\right]}{{X}_{S} + \left[X\right]}$

Case-1: $\left[X\right] > > {X}_{s}; \left[X\right] + {X}_{s} \approx \left[X\right]$

rate $= \dfrac{k\left[X\right]}{\left[X\right]} = k$ (Zero order w.r.t. $X$)

$I \to P, S$

Case-2: $\left[X\right] ≪ {X}_{s}; \left[X\right] + {X}_{s} \approx {X}_{s}$

$∴$ rate $= \dfrac{k\left[X\right]}{{X}_{S}} = {k}^{'}\left[X\right]$ (${1}^{st}$ order w.r.t. $X$)

$∴ I \to Q, T$

Case-3: $\left[X\right] \approx {X}_{S}$

rate $= \dfrac{k\left[X\right]}{{X}_{s} + \left[X\right]}$

In this case curve-$R$ given in List-II will match.

$∴ I \to P, Q, R, S, T$ (The graph of half-life should start from origin)

$\left(II\right)$ rate $= \dfrac{k\left[X\right]}{{X}_{S} + \left[X\right]}$

$∵ \left[X\right] ≪ {X}_{S}$

$∴ {X}_{s} + \left[X\right] \approx {X}_{s}$

$∴$ rate $= \dfrac{k\left[X\right]}{{X}_{S}} = {k}^{'}\left[X\right]$ (${1}^{st}$ order w.r.t. $X$)

$∴ II \to Q, T$

$\left(III\right)$ rate $= \dfrac{k\left[X\right]}{{X}_{s} + \left[X\right]}$

$∵ \left[X\right] > > {X}_{s}$

$∴ {X}_{s} + \left[X\right] \approx \left[X\right]$

$∴$ rate $= \dfrac{k\left[X\right]}{\left[X\right]} = k$ (Zero order w.r.t. $X$)

$∴ III \to P, S$

$\left(IV\right)$ rate $= \dfrac{k{\left[X\right]}^{2}}{{X}_{s} + \left[X\right]}$

$∵ \left[X\right] > > {X}_{S}$

$∴ {X}_{S} + \left[X\right] \approx \left[X\right]$

$∴$ rate $= \dfrac{k{\left[X\right]$}^{2}}{$\left[X\right]$} = k $\left[X\right]$ (${1}^{st}$ order w.r.t. $X$)

$∴ IV \to Q, T$

questions.q: For the first order reaction $2 \mathrm{~N}_2 \mathrm{O}_5(\mathrm{~g}) \longrightarrow 4 \mathrm{NO}_2(g)+\mathrm{O}_2(g)$
options:
the concentration of the reactant decreases exponentially with time.

the half-life of the reaction decreases with increasing temperature

the half-life of the reaction depends on the initial concentration of the reactant.

the reaction proceeds of $99.6 \%$ completion in eight half-life duration.
questions.solution: (a) For a first order reaction, the concentration of reactant remaining after time $t$ is given by $[A]=[A]_0 e^{-k t}$ Therefore, concentration of reactant decreases exponentially with time. (b) Rise in temperature increases rate constant $(k)$ and therefore decreases half-life $\left(t_{1 / 2}\right)$ as t_{1 / 2}=$\frac{\operatorname{In} 2}{k}$ \\ (d) For a first order reaction, if 100 moles of reactant is taken initially, after $n$ half-lives, reactant remaining is given by $\begin{aligned}$& $\text{ Percentage }$A=100$\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^$n=100$\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^$8=0.3906 \\ & \Rightarrow $\text{ A reacted }=$100-0.3906=99.6 \% \end{aligned} (c) Half-life of first order reaction is independent of initial concentration.
questions.question: For the first order reaction $2 \mathrm{~N}_2 \mathrm{O}_5(\mathrm{~g}) \longrightarrow 4 \mathrm{NO}_2(g)+\mathrm{O}_2(g)$

questions.q:
For a first order reaction, $A \rightarrow P$, the temperature $(T)$ dependent rate constant $(k)$ was found to follow the equation, $\log k=-(2000) / T+6.0$
The pre-exponential factor $A$ and the activation energy $\left(E_a\right)$, respectively, are
questions.solution:
Comparing the slope and intercept of the given equation with the following Arrhenius equation :
$$
\log k=-\frac{E_a}{2303 R T}+\log A
$$
Hence, $\log A=6$ i.e. $A=10^6 \mathrm{~s}^{-1}$.
Comparing slope gives $E_a=38.3 \mathrm{~kJ} / \mathrm{mol}$.

questions.explanation:
All radioactive decays are the examples of first order kinetics.
So, decay constant $\lambda=\frac{1}{T_1-T_2} \ln \frac{C_1}{C_2}$
$C_1$ is the concentration at $T_1$ time
$C_2$ is the concentration at $T_2$ time
So, $\quad T_1-T_2=\frac{1}{\lambda} \ln \frac{C_1}{C_2}$
